headline: A UK watchdog says AI-generated child sexual abuse imagery it found in the first half of 2026 already exceeds the whole of last year.
score_reason: Pool score kept: clear monitor data, but a trend report rather than a single event.
importance_line: Children, and families who share pictures of them online, face growing risk, and the figures raise pressure on the UK government and AI companies for binding rules, which ministers have not yet announced.
summary: The Guardian reports that the Internet Watch Foundation, a UK charity that monitors abuse material worldwide, assessed 6,310 AI-generated images meeting the legal definition of child sexual abuse in the first half of 2026, 40% more than the whole of 2025. The charity says this shows the need for binding AI legislation, while the government points to existing bans on AI models built to produce such material and has not signalled a new bill.
notes: Sensitive subject; kept factual, no description of content.
